text.p: Chris Gomez's two-out single in the 10th inning scored Greg Vaughn with the winning run as the San Diego Padres beat the Pittsburgh Pirates 3-2 Monday.

Vaughn drew a one-out walk off Matt Ruebel (1-1). Wally Joyner followed with a bloop single to left to advance Vaughn to second. After John Flaherty flied to short centre, Gomez singled into shallow left-centre for his second extra-inning, game-winning hit of the season.

"When you do get (a chance) you just try to relax as much as possible, see the ball and put it in play somewhere," Gomez said. "I'm always confident, even when I've been struggling, that the next time up I'll hit the ball hard."
Dario Veras (1-0) got the victory after pitching a scoreless 10th inning. He came on to start the 10th after Trevor Hoffman gave up the tying run in the ninth on Mark Johnson's RBI single.
San Diego had taken a 2-1 lead in the bottom of the eighth. Tony Gwynn doubled to deep left centre with one out and scored when Steve Finley followed with a double to deep right centre.
"It was great that we were able to come back and still have a chance," Pittsburgh manager Gene Lamont said. "If you're a fan that likes pitching duels, it was a hell of a ball game."
The Padres loaded the bases in the bottom of the ninth. but Ruebel retired Finley to get out of the inning.
Both starters breezed through the first five innings before Ken Caminiti drove a 1-0 pitch from Jon Lieber into right field for his second homer of the season and a 1-0 San Diego lead.
Pittsburgh tied it in the eighth when Joe Randa singled home Kendall, who had singled with one out.
Lieber and San Diego starter Andy Ashby both pitched well before earning their second no decisions of the season.

In Los Angeles, Brett Butler, who was not supposed to play after being diagnosed with a swollen lymph node, scored from second base on an infield single by Tom Prince in the bottom of the 15th inning as the Dodgers edged the New York Mets 3-2.

Butler, who saw a throat specialist Monday who determined he was suffering from the swollen node and mouth sores, entered the game in the ninth inning. After a pair of walks in his first two at-bats, he just beat out a fielder's choice groundball in the 15th.
He stole second against Mets reliever Joe Crawford (0-1) with two outs and came around to score when Prince bounced to first baseman John Olerud.
Olerud, who ranged into the hole, threw a little behind Crawford, who was just beaten to the bag by Prince. Butler never stopped and scored the winning run without a throw.
Crawford's loss came in his first major-league appearance as New York used six relievers.
Pedro Astacio (1-0), normally a starter, earned the victory with three scoreless innings in relief.
Todd Hundley hit a two-run homer for New York in the sixth. After the Dodgers pecked out a pair of runs in the eighth to knot the score, the teams traded scoreless frames until the 15th.
New York starter Mark Clark allowed two runs and five hits in 7 1/3 innings, walking three and striking out three.
Dodger starter Hideo Nomo allowed two runs and three hits in six innings against the Mets, one of two teams he doesn't own a career winning record against.

In Colorado, Vinny Castilla and Jeff Reed belted three-run homers and every starter had at least one hit, including pitcher Bill Swift, as the Rockies celebrated their home opener with a 13-2 blowout of the Cincinnati Reds Monday.
The Rockies have won five straight and scored at least five runs in each game during the winning streak.
Swift (1-1) gave up three hits and two runs -- one earned -- with two walks and four strikeouts in six innings.

Dave Burba (1-1) was ripped for 10 runs -- all earned -- and 10 hits with three walks in just 3 1/3 innings. Cincinnati suffered its fourth loss in five games.
In San Francisco, Shawn Estes allowed two runs over 5 2/3 innings and Rod Beck tossed a scoreless ninth for his fourth save as the Giants edged the Philadelphia Phillies, 4-3.

Estes allowed just four hits, walking four and striking out four. Julian Tavarez, Rich Rodriguez and Doug Henry held the Phillies to just a run and two hits over the next 2 1/3 innings before Beck closed the game in the ninth.
Calvin Maduro (0-2) took the loss.
Jeff Kent had a pair of RBI for the Giants, who have won four of their last five after dropping the season opener.
